items.title: A `void` `main` whose TAIL is a void-typed expression - a `match` of void arms, a call written with no `;` (`print("x")`) - is emitted on JS with `process.exit(<tail>)` after it, ending the process while a spawned task is still pending: `async { time::sleep(50); print("done"); }; match 2 { 1 => .., _ => print("tail") }` prints only `tail` on JS and both lines natively
items.body: transformer.rs decides main's disposition SYNTACTICALLY: a tail that is `Expr::Void` (or none) is discarded, anything else is forwarded to `process.exit` as the exit code (`undefined` here, so exit 0). A void-typed tail expression therefore takes the exit path, and `process.exit` drops the event loop's queued work (a spawned task's timer, an idle-but-referenced handle). The native backend waits for the work (`run_pending`/`block_on`), so the two backends print different bytes for a check-clean program; `if` tails and `print(..);` with its semicolon are fine. Rec: decide by the tail's TYPE (void/unit -> discard; a non-void `i32` tail -> the exit code), pin both shapes (`match`, a `;`-less call) on both backends with a pending spawned task. Estate: count kolt's/the website's/the examples' `fun main` with a void tail expression before calling it `miscompile` vs `breaking` (a program relying on the early exit would change). Met while pinning A173 S1's held-open stdin: the emitted exit hid the JS pump's missing `unref` (the pin's `main` now ends on a plain statement).

items.title: A native program parked on `read_line`/`prompt` burns CPU while it waits: ~0.12 s of CPU per 5 s of a silent, open stdin (~2.4 %, debug build) against node's 0.00 s - the executor polls its I/O sources every `IO_POLL_INTERVAL` (1 ms) while any source is live
items.body: A173 S1's stdin source is live only while a read waits (so an idle stdin costs nothing), but a human typing a line is exactly that wait, and the executor's turn model sleeps 1 ms between polls when no timer is due (R8: no epoll without libc). terminal.md §5.2 names the refinement: when stdin is the ONLY live source, block on the reader's channel with `recv_timeout` until the next timer deadline (or indefinitely with no timer) instead of sleeping 1 ms; the same shape serves S2's key stream, where the wait is the program's whole life. Measure with the probe's idle.py (native release and debug) before and after; no ordering change (the poll answers the same chunk, only sooner and without the spin).

items.title: SIGTERM to `vilan run` does not reach the program it started: node (or the native binary) keeps running, orphaned - a supervisor, an editor task or a harness that stops `vilan run` leaves a server holding its port or a program parked on stdin; and a child killed by a signal is reported as exit 1, not 128+signal
items.body: `vilan run` waits with `Command::status()` (`exit_code_of`) and handles no signal, so only Ctrl-C in a terminal (SIGINT to the whole foreground group) stops both. Rec: forward SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT to the child and wait for it (unix; on Windows the job-object equivalent so a killed `vilan run` takes its child), and map a signal death to 128+n as a shell does. Pin: start `vilan run` on a program parked on `read_line`, SIGTERM it, assert the child is gone. Check what `--watch` already does for its rounds before building (it restarts children itself). Met by std-54's stdin harness: a red step's kill of `vilan run` left the native binary running.
